261: Penance means two things: bearing your own hardships, and never giving pain to others.
262: Only those made strong by past practice can bear penance. Without that groundwork, the attempt is in vain.
263: Some set aside their own strict disciplines so that those who have renounced everything may eat.
264: If the ascetic wishes harm to enemies or good to friends, their discipline has the power even for that.
265: Discipline practiced in this world secures whatever one hopes to enjoy in the next.
266: Those who do penance do their duty. All others, tangled in desire, work their own ruin.
267: As gold glows brighter for the fire, so shine those who have burned in repeated penance.
268: Every creature will bow in worship to the one who has mastered their own soul.
269: Those who gain the power of discipline can even step past the boundary of Death himself.
270: Few discipline themselves and many do not — that is why the world holds many destitute and few rich.
271: Even the five elements within him laugh at the faker's pretend-holiness.
272: What use is a holy show tall as the sky, if the mind secretly holds to sin?
273: Power shown without power within is a cow grazing in a tiger's skin.
274: Whoever wears the ascetic's mask to commit sins is like a hunter hiding in the thicket to net birds.
275: The false pose of renunciation will one day bring sorrows that make them cry: "What have we done! What have we done!"
276: None alive are harder of heart than those who keep their desires hidden under a renouncer's dress.
277: Some are bright as the rosary-berry outside and black as its seed within.
278: Many wear a mask of holiness — bathing and performing rites for the world to see.
279: The arrow looks straight and bends from its mark; the lute looks bent and makes straight music. Judge people by their deeds, not their looks.
280: No shaven crown or matted hair is needed, if only one avoids the deeds the wise condemn.
281: Whoever refuses to be despised must keep the mind from cheating another of the smallest thing.
282: Even the thought of sin is sin. Do not even think of cleverly stealing another's property.
283: Wealth gained by fraud perishes entirely, even while it seems to grow.
284: The craving to cheat, when it bears fruit, bears undying sorrow.
285: There is no kindness in the person who waits for another's forgetfulness to seize his wealth.
286: Those greedy to defraud others cannot walk steadily in any right path.
287: The crooked cunning called fraud never enters the heart that wants the greatness called honesty.
288: Deceit sits in the cheat's mind the way goodness sits in the honest person's.
289: Those who know nothing but fraud will perish in the very act of it.
290: Even their bodies desert the cheats; but even heaven does not desert the honest.
292: Even a falsehood takes the nature of truth if it brings a benefit with no fault in it.
294: Whoever keeps a mind free of deceit will live in the hearts of all people.
295: Whoever speaks truth with their whole heart stands above those who give gifts and do penance.
296: No praise equals the praise of never lying. It harms no one and leads to every virtue.
298: Water cleans the body. Truth cleans the mind.
299: Not every lamp is truly a lamp. The lamp of truth is the lamp of the wise.
300: Of every excellence we have seen described, none is so good as truthfulness.
301: Controlling anger counts when it can wound. When it cannot, control or not, it little matters.
302: Anger is bad even when it can do nothing. When it can do something, there is no greater evil.
303: Let go of anger toward everyone. Every evil springs from it.
304: What other foe does a person such harm as anger does?
306: The fire of anger burns up even the pleasant raft of friendship.
307: Anger cherished as a friend brings destruction, as sure as a hand slaps the earth.
308: Even if someone drops a burning bundle on you, hold your anger, if you can.
309: The heart that never hosts anger sees its wishes granted at once.
310: The rageful are as good as dead. The anger-free are as good as immortal.
311: The spotless have made up their minds: they will not cause sorrow to others even to win the wealth that crowns a person.
312: The spotless have resolved: no evil in return, even to those who hated them and harmed them.
315: What good has his knowledge done him, who does not try to keep pain off others as much as off himself?
317: The chief of all virtues: never knowingly doing evil to any person, in the least degree, at any time.
318: Why do we give other creatures the very pains we know from our own experience are pains?
319: Bring sorrow to others in the morning, and by evening it returns to you, unasked.
320: Pain returns to those who cause pain. So those who wish to be free of sorrow cause none.
321: Never killing is the heart of all good conduct. Killing opens the door to every evil.
322: Of all virtues ever written down, the chiefest are these: to share your food and spare all life.
323: Not taking life is the greatest good. Next to it stands freedom from falsehood.
324: The right path is the one that searches for every way not to kill.
325: Of all who renounce the world, the chiefest is the one who trembles to kill even the smallest life.
326: Death itself will not attack the life of the one firmly set on never destroying life.
327: Let no one take another's life — even if it should cost them their own.
328: Even if a sacrifice promised great good, the killing in it would shame the wise.
329: Those who deal in murder are of savage deeds. Their baseness is plain to any heart that knows what vileness is.
330: The wise say: those who now live sick and destitute once stripped the life from other creatures.
332: Getting wealth is like a crowd gathering for a show. Spending it is like the crowd dispersing.
333: Wealth does not last. Turn it at once into deeds that do.
335: Do your good deeds quickly, before the last hiccup silences the tongue.
336: Such is this world's greatness: whoever was here yesterday is not here today.
337: The unwise fill their minds with countless plans, not knowing if they will live another moment.
338: The soul's love for the body is like a bird's love for its egg — one day it flies away and leaves it empty.
339: Death is like falling asleep. Birth is like waking from it.
340: It seems the soul only lodges for a while in the body — as if it never found a true home.
341: Whatever a person has renounced, by that thing they can be hurt no more.
342: Even after giving things up, temptations remain. If they pull you, renounce more deeply while there is time.
343: Let the five senses' pull be destroyed, and at once let go everything you once desired.
344: Having nothing is the ascetic's proper state. Possessions bend the will and drag back the old confusion.
345: When even the body is one burden too many for the renouncer, why take on anything else?
346: Whoever cuts off the pride of 'I' and 'mine' enters a world higher than the gods'.
347: Sorrows never let go of those who do not let go of desire.
348: The fully renounced have reached the shore. All others wander, caught in the net of endless births.
349: The instant desire dies, rebirth is cut. Until it dies, all is unstable.
350: To end desire, desire only this: the desireless desire of the One without desire.
351: Low births come from the confusion that takes unreal things to be real.
352: Clear, true sight of things lifts one out of the dark of rebirth into bliss.
353: For the pure of mind and free of doubt, heaven is nearer than earth.
354: Even all that the five senses can teach is useless without knowing the true nature of things.
355: True knowledge is to see each thing as the true thing it is.
356: Those who in this birth come to know the True Being enter the road that returns no more to this world.
357: For the one who has truly known the Real, do not imagine another birth.
358: True knowledge: removing the ignorance that causes rebirth, and seeing the Real that gives heaven.
359: Whoever lives to know the Support of all and abandon all desire will be freed from the evils that would cling and spoil their striving.
360: Destroy the very names of desire, anger, and confusion, and the evils born of them die with them.
361: The seed that keeps every creature being born, age after age, the wise say, is desire.
362: If you must desire anything, desire freedom from birth — and that comes by desiring to be without desire.
364: Purity of mind is freedom from desire, and that freedom is the fruit of loving truth.
365: Only those freed of desire are called free. Whatever else they may be free of, the rest are not.
366: Fear desire like a lurking enemy. It can deceive and destroy even the careful.
367: Cut desire off at the root, and deeds that never fail will meet you on every path.
369: Destroy desire — that sorrow of sorrows — and joy never leaves the mind, even in this body.
370: Uproot the desire that is never satisfied, and you gain a state that can never be shaken.
371: A kind fate gives perseverance; a cruel fate, laziness.
372: Bad fate turns learning to folly; good fate turns folly to learning.
373: However much one studies, what fate has written will still rule the mind.
374: Fate deals two natures among people; that is why fortunes and learning differ.
375: Through fate's power, everything favorable turns unfavorable, and everything unfavorable turns favorable, in the winning of wealth.
376: What fate has not given cannot be kept, however painfully you guard it. What fate has given cannot be lost, though you throw it away.
377: Even the hoarder of millions enjoys only the share allotted to them.
378: Even the very poor would turn ascetics — if fate let them live out their days unhindered.
380: What is stronger than fate? Even as you scheme against it, it is there ahead of you.
